Stated Claim / Post Context:
California Botox doctor used $45 million in Medicare money to fund her lavish lifestyle, feds say

Violetta Mailyan was convicted in May of billing Botox injections that were never provided.

Actual Article Body:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.

See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search.   Set us as preferred

A Glendale doctor who fraudulently billed more than $45 million in Botox injections to Medicare and used the proceeds to fund a lavish lifestyle was sentenced Thursday to 15 years in federal prison.

Violetta Mailyan, 45, was convicted in May of nine counts of wire fraud and three counts of obstruction of an investigation of a healthcare offense, as she attempted to mislead federal agents. Prosecutors said Mailyan was involved in an elaborate fraud scheme that ignored Medicare’s rules for Botox coverage and brazenly fabricated medical records.

Mailyan was the owner-operator of Healthy Way Medical Center, a clinic that claimed to provide beauty and cosmetic services, according to the Department of Justice press office. A federal probe by the Office of Inspector General and the FBI presented evidence that found Mailyan billed and received Medicare payments for thousands of Botox injections that were never provided.

California

Prosecutors allege the Glendale-based doctor submitted more than $45 million in fraudulent Medicare claims for Botox injections, using the payments to fund a lavish lifestyle.

“Mailyan also billed for providing Botox injections when she was actually on vacation in Mexico, Hawaii, Las Vegas, Pennsylvania, and New York at various times throughout her fraud scheme,” the Justice Department said. “For example, Mailyan billed over $200,000 for purportedly providing Botox services to patients in California when she was actually relaxing on the beach in Cabo.”

Prosecutors said when federal investigators were closing in, Mailyan falsified medical records and forged Medicare beneficiary signatures, including for a man in federal prison during the time the doctor claimed to have provided treatment.

The investigation also found that Mailyan used the Medicare payments to fund many of the vacations she took and purchase luxury collectibles such as a $12,000 17th-century crossbow and a $3,000 painting, prosecutors said.

The jury that convicted Mailyan also determined that several of her assets were proceeds of the fraud scheme and subject to forfeiture, including a Tesla Cybertruck, four properties in Surfside and Glendale worth more than $7 million total, more than $250,000 in multiple bank accounts and brokerage accounts valued at $7 million, according to the Justice Department.

In addition to the prison sentence, the court ordered the immediate forfeiture of more than $16 million worth of property seized from Mailyan, including real property, personal property and securities, and to pay $32 million in restitution to Medicare.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

(Oct. 30, 2026 / JNS) A California man pleaded guilty on Friday to trying to provide material support to ISIS, according to the US Justice Department.

Ammaad Akhtar, 34, tried to funnel money, weapons and other equipment to the terror organization between February 2025 and June 2025 when he was in contact with an undercover officer, whom he believed to be an ISIS member, the department said.

Akhtar faces up to 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

In those communications, he said that he wanted to join ISIS and to “die in the cause of Allah fighting the kuffar,” Arabic for “infidels,” and asked for directions to build a bomb to “make a boom” at a crowded event.

Akhtar met with an undercover agent in June 2025 and “provided clothing, binoculars, $400 cash, two loaded guns and six additional magazines” and pledged loyalty to ISIS.

His sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 26, 2027.
